Hi James — thanks for the note and the attachments. Sorry to hear about the delta; we take invoicing clarity seriously. Quick response while I pull Monica in for the deep details:

1) Short answer on tool output: hosted billing attributes tokens produced by tools to the same request as the model response; tool outputs are billed as output tokens (they appear on the IO breakdown).
2) System prompts: by default counted per request (i.e., every API call that includes the system prompt will be counted). There are caching behaviors for Dedicated/Private but not on Hosted by default.
3) Rounding: hosted invoices round token usage per request to the nearest token bucket according to the configured granularity (we historically round up at the request level).

That said, the precise behavior can vary by endpoint (streaming vs. synchronous) and whether the tool call emits incremental streamed tokens. I'm looping Monica (serving/runtime) and Laura (pricing) to provide a worked example and confirm whether any batched rounding or post-aggregation adjustments could explain ~18%.

—Rishi

Hi all — adding the technical breakdown and an explicit example so James' team can reconcile against their meter. I kept the example conservative and matched the counts James asked for.

High-level rules (hosted API, current rate card behavior):
- Token attribution: each request's tokens are split into input (user+system+context) and output (model tokens + any tool-returned text). Tool calls are considered part of the response pipeline; any tokens produced by the tool (text returned to the model or user) are billed as output tokens for that request.
- System prompts: billed as input tokens for every individual API request that includes them. There is no implicit session-level amortization on hosted endpoints unless the customer opts into our prefix-caching addon (not default).
- Streaming and incremental tool output: when streaming is used, we count tokens as they are produced; billing rounds per-request after tokenization, not per-stream-chunk.
- Rounding: we round up at the request level to the nearest whole token. There is no later global prorating that reduces the sum — invoice = sum(round_per_request(tokens)). This behavior explains persistent upward deltas versus meters that tally fractional tokens before rounding.

Worked example (exact sequence):
- System prompt: 120 tokens (included in every request)
- 8 user messages total, average 18 tokens each => 144 input tokens spread across 8 requests
- 8 assistant responses, average 60 tokens each => 480 model output tokens
- 6 tool calls during the conversation, tool returns average 40 tokens each => 240 tool-output tokens (billed as output)

Per-request accounting (simplified):
Assume a pattern where each user message triggers one assistant response; some assistant responses trigger tool calls within the same request. For requests without a tool call:
- Input = system(120) + user(~18) = ~138 => rounded to 138 tokens
- Output = assistant(~60) => rounded to 60 tokens
For requests with a tool call (tool output included in the response request):
- Input = system(120) + user(18) = ~138 => 138
- Output = assistant(60) + tool(40) = 100 => 100

If you run the math across the 8 requests with 6 of them including tool calls (6 tool responses, 2 no-tool requests):
- Total input (before rounding): system repeated 8x => 960 + user 144 = 1104 input tokens
- After per-request rounding input stays 1104 (system and user already whole tokens in this example)
- Total output before rounding: assistant 480 + tool 240 = 720 output tokens
- After per-request rounding (round up output per request), small per-request increases accumulate. For example, if some assistant responses were 59.4 -> round to 60, or tool output tokenization differences occur, the per-request rounding adds up.

Bottom line: rounding per-request (and treating tool output as output tokens) is the main source of an upward delta compared to a meter that sums fractional tokens across the session and only rounds at the end.

What you can do / next steps:
- If Atlas prefers session-level amortization, we can quote a custom hosted billing profile that rounds at the session level for committed customers (this requires a signed SLA/commitment).
- We can also enable prefix-caching for persistent system prompts to avoid counting the same system prompt on every request (saves ~system_token_count * requests). That is typically a Dedicated/Private feature but available as an add-on in hosted for contracts > X commit.

I can produce an export that shows per-request rounding deltas for the sample period (it will list original fractional counts, rounded value, and delta). Rishi — do you want me to attach that to the formal response?

—Monica
